newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Gilt charts call for dip after Labour win.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Gilt charts call for dip after Labour win.

text.p: LIFFE June gilt futures face tough resistance at 110-28 to 111-00 on Friday, and are likely to slip back near term, technical analysts said.
Much of the Labour Party victory at the British election has already been priced into the market and the pressure will be for gilts to correct back, they said.
"Technically 110-28 is a very difficult long-term resistnace barrier, so in the short term the risk is to the downside," said David Wood, an independant technical analyst near London.
"But the fact that it has been such a big victory will give certainty to the market so the downside is probably limited, and that fits in with the charts at the moment."
Wood said for Friday's session, while the contract was below 110-28, there was an inital support area at 110-14, 10.
That area incorporates hourly supports and the April 17 high.
"If you eat into that then I would expect the next area at 109-27 to 109-21 to hold it. That probably would represent good value for the market," he said.
But he said the U.S. April employment report, due at 1230 GMT, could knock T-bonds and affect gilts and T-bonds.
David Sneddon, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London,also saw good resistance in the 110-28 to 111-00 area.
"A lot of this is very much in the market and the pressure is going to be on the gilt to come off and correct the strong gains we have had over the past week," he said.
The immediate pressure is for gilts to hold up or to come in slightly lower and not to see 111-00 violated, he said.
June gilt futures closed at 110-25 on Thursday having opened at 110-23.

"Only if the market comes back below 109-16 today can you say that it is possibly the end of this whole corrective movement and that gilts are going to try and test that big 108-05, 108-00 area again," said Sneddon.
If gilts do succeed in breaking to the upside, Wood said there was little to halt a rise until 111-16.
